## Natural history notes

A crustose lichen characterized by a thin olive-gray to greenish-brown thallus with small embedded fruiting structures that may appear as tiny dark dots or slightly raised bumps on the surface. In Florida, it is found growing on smooth tree bark in humid wooded habitats such as hammocks, swamps, shaded forests, and other moist subtropical areas where bark-dwelling lichens are common. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, growing tightly attached to bark and absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on other organisms.
